question: What mistakes do military buyers make when buying a home in Hampton Roads?
answer: The common ones are choosing by commute alone, skipping flood and military noise-zone checks, setting a payment without comparing it to BAH, and not planning for resale or renting after a PCS. Check each before you make an offer.
answer_short: Choosing by commute alone, skipping flood and noise-zone checks, ignoring BAH math, and not planning for resale or renting.
description: Common mistakes military and VA buyers make in Hampton Roads, from flood and noise zones to BAH math and resale planning, and how to avoid each.
body:
Here's the deal: a PCS clock makes people rush, and rushing is where the expensive mistakes happen. You have a short window, so get clarity early and move fast on the right things.

The Mistakes to Avoid

  1. Choosing by commute alone. Test the drive at the hours you will actually drive it, including any bridge or tunnel crossings.
  2. Skipping the flood check. Look up the exact address on FEMA's flood map and get an insurance quote before your inspection period ends. See whether you need flood insurance.
  3. Ignoring military noise zones. Learn what the noise-zone disclosure says and visit the home at different times of day.
  4. Not running the BAH math. Put the full monthly cost, including tax, insurance and any flood policy, next to your BAH with the VA loan payment calculator.
  5. Not planning the exit. You may be moving again in a few years. Think about resale and about whether renting the home out is allowed by your loan terms and any HOA rules.
  6. Shopping before you are pre-approved. Talk to a VA-experienced lender first so you know your real budget and funding fee.

Use the buyer checklist as your game plan. This is general information, not legal or financial advice; confirm loan rules with your lender.
faqs: Can I rent out my VA-financed home after a PCS?
Many service members do, but loan occupancy rules, HOA rules and local requirements apply. Ask your lender and read the HOA documents before you buy.
Should I buy or rent for a short tour?
It depends on how long you expect to stay, local prices and your finances. Run the full monthly cost against your BAH and talk with a lender before deciding.
